instruction: To help the study team identify questions in this phone script, please underline all sentences that end with a question mark.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires underlining sentences that end with question marks. From the document, there are at least 5 question sentences (e.g., 'Is this an Ok time for you to speak?', 'Would you like to hear more about this study?', etc.). The evaluator checks if at least 5 underlined texts end with question marks.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete coverage: Instruction requires underlining ALL sentences ending with '?', but evaluator only checks if at least 5 questions are underlined (using min_questions=5 threshold)
No verification of completeness: If document has 7 questions but user only underlines 5, the task incorrectly passes despite incomplete work
No penalty for over-underlining: Evaluator doesn't check that ONLY question sentences are underlined - user could underline non-question text and still pass

Potential partial text issue: Getter extracts underlined spans, but if a question sentence spans multiple formatting elements and only part is underlined, the extracted text might not include the '?' and would be missed
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change approach: Instead of counting underlined questions, the evaluator should: (1) identify ALL sentences in the document ending with '?', (2) verify each one is underlined, (3) verify no non-question text is underlined
Alternative metric logic: Check that the set of underlined texts exactly matches the set of question sentences (with proper sentence boundary detection)
Add document analysis: Parse the full document text to identify all question sentences, then verify one-to-one correspondence with underlined texts
Consider full-sentence extraction: Ensure getter captures complete sentences, not just underlined spans that might be partial
